1) Data residency: our default hosting for hosted customers in US regions is US-only; will confirm residency clauses with Markus and flag any exceptions.
2) SOC 2: attaching a short SOC2-summary.pdf that covers our current coverage; Markus, can you advise if a full report needs to be shared or if a letter suffices for pilot?

- I'll set up a 30-min sync with your procurement to finalize billing cadence and start dates.

Camila / Alex — thanks. I did a quick scan of the MSA you shared. High-level intake comments:

- Data residency: MSA currently references region-based hosting; will add an explicit US-only residency addendum for the pilot and produce language for both the MSA and an Exhibit A if you want it tied to the order form.
- Liability cap: Granite's draft has a per-claim cap equal to annual fees; we typically propose a lower cap for pilots. I'll mark the clause and propose a compromise (2x pilot value) in the redline.
- Indemnity / IP: standard carveouts are acceptable but need clearer scope for model-derived outputs.
- Security evidence: SOC2-summary.pdf is helpful. For procurement we usually provide a SOC 2 Type II report under NDA or a SOC 2 letter. Laura: please prepare an NDA template for sharing the full report if needed.

I plan to deliver a tracked redline (MSA_Granite_Redline_MK.docx) by end of day tomorrow. Camila: if there are commercial levers you already agreed on (discounts, pilot seat counts), add them so I can reconcile the liability and termination windows.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Senior Counsel | Redwood Inference
